questions.question: Which of the following is not a physical quantity?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• A physical quantity is a property of a material. It can be expressed in number by measurement.
 
• A physical quantity is expressed by a numerical value and a unit. For example, the physical quantity length can be expressed as 4 meters, where 4 is the numerical value and meter is the unit.
 
• The SI units are the standard units of measurement defined by the International System of Units (SI).

EXPLANATION:__

 
• Following are the SI units of the physical quantity:

 

 
 

 **Physical Quantity**
 **SI Units**
 
 

 Power
 watt
 
 

 Inductance
 henry
 
 

 Capacitance
 farad
 
 

 Force
 newton
 
 

 Mass
 kilogram
 
 

 Resistance
 ohm
 
 

 Energy, work
 joule
 
 

 

The **kilogram represents the unit of a physical quantity** and **not the physical quantity**. Therefore option 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49db1e88466c4075382b1073285f91a9ab0332e48bb5db4e537f337fc9ab0472.png] 

 
• The name and symbol of SI units are written in lowercase.
 
• Except for the symbols of those SI units, named after a person, which are written with an initial capital letter.
 
• For example, the second has the symbol s, but the kelvin has the symbol K because it is named after Lord Kelvin.

questions.question: Dimensional formula of magnetic flux is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. M1 I-1 L2 T-2

**__CONCEPT__**:

__
 
• **Magnetic flux:** Magnetic flux is the measure of the number of magnetic field lines passing through a given surface area.

The magnetic flux ϕ is given by:

ϕ = BAcosθ 

Where B is the magnetic field strength, A is the area vector, and θ is the angle made by the area vector with respect to the magnetic field line.

**EXPLANATION**__:

We know, ϕ = BAcosθ 

For dimensional analysis, ϕ = BA

The dimensional formula of A (area) = L² ----(1)

From lenz's law we know that F = q(v × B) ⇒ B = (F)/(qv)

Force, F = mass × acceleration ⇒ M¹ L¹T⁻² ----(2)

Charge, q = Current × time ⇒ I¹ T¹ ----(3)

Velocity, v ⇒ L¹ T⁻¹ ----(4)

Substituting (1), (2), (3), and (4) in ϕ = BA

**[ϕ] **= (F)/(qv)A = frac{M¹ L¹T⁻² }{(I¹T¹)(L¹T⁻¹)} L² = **M1 I-1 L2 T-2**

questions.question: Unit of Gravitational constant in S.I. system is:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Universal Gravitational Constant (G): It is a relating force to mass and distance in Newton’s laws of gravitation.

__
 
• Its value is 6.67408 × 10-11 m3 kg-1 s-2 in SI Unit.
 
• The law of Gravitation states, the force between two bodies is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely to the square of their distance between them.

Newton’s law of gravitation: Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force, which is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to square of distance between them.

Where, F = force of attraction, G = 6.67 × 10-11 N-m2/kg2 (gravitational constant), m1 & m2 = mass of bodies, r = distance between them.

 
• Unit of ‘G’ is Nm2/kg2 or Nm2kg-2. Dimensional formula of ‘G’ is [M-1L3T-2].

questions.question: The force (F) acting on a body varies with displacement x as F = ax² + bx + c. Find the dimensional formula of b. (a, b and c are constants).
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__**:**

__
 
• Principle of homogeneity of dimensions: According to this principle, a physical equation will be dimensionally correct if the dimensions of all the terms occurring on both sides of the equation are the same.

 
 
• This principle is based on the fact that only the physical quantities of the same kind can be added, subtracted, or compared.
 
• Thus, the velocity can be added to velocity but not to force.
 
 

EXPLANATION__**:**

Given that:

F = ax2 + bx + c

 
• From the principle of dimensional homogeneity, the left-hand side of the equation dimensionally equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

The dimensional formula of Force (F) = [M L T⁻²]

The dimensional formula of Displacement (x) = [L]

LHS = RHS

[M L T-2] = [b] × [L]

[b] = M L⁰ T⁻²

Hence option 4 is correct.

Where, I = impulse, F = force and dt = very small time interval.

questions.question: Which of the following has unit but no dimension?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Angle__.

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The powers to which fundamental quantities must be raised in order to express the given physical quantity are called its dimensions.
 
• A quantity without dimension will usually be a ratio of two quantities with similar dimensions and hence, will cancel out. Thus, they will have no units.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• Velocity: It is defined as the rate of change of displacement i.e.

Rightarrow Velocity = (Displacemnt)/(Time)=([L])/([T])=[LT⁻¹]

 
• Velocity is not the dimensionless quantity and unit of velocity is** m/s**.
 
• Angle: It is defined as the ratio of the length of arc to the radius, i.e.,

​Angle ( theta ) = frac{{length of arc ( l )}}{{radius ( r )}}

 Rightarrow theta = frac{{[ {{M⁰}L{T⁰}} ]}}{{[ {{M⁰}L{T⁰}} ]}} = 1

 
• An angle is a dimensionless quantity and the unit of angle is **rad**.
 
• Mass is a **not** dimensionless quantity and the** unit of mass is kg**.
 
• The time is a not dimensionless quantity and the unit of time is sec.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of units are used for measuring the same physical quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m2/s2, Ws.**__

**__Explanation:__**

**kg m²/s² and Ws:**

__
 
• These units are equivalent and measure the same physical quantity. kg m²/s² is a unit of energy (joule, J), and Ws (watt-second) is also a unit of energy.
 
• They **both measure energy.**

**kg m/s² and Nm:**

 
• These units are not exactly the same, but they are related.
 
• kg m/s² represents force (Newton, N), and Nm represents torque, which is a type of rotational force.
 
• While they have a connection, they don't directly measure the same quantity.

**kg m/s² and Ws:**

 
• These units are not the same and measure different quantities.
 
• kg m/s² represents force (Newton, N), while Ws (watt-second) is a unit of energy.

**kg m²/s² and J/s:**

 
• These units are not the same and measure different quantities.
 
• kg m²/s² represents energy (joule, J), whereas J/s represents power (watt, W), which is the rate of energy transfer.

Thus, **the pair of units that are used for measuring the same physical quantity are kg m²/s² and Ws.**__

questions.question: Which physical unit is defined as the field intensity that produces one newton (N) of force per ampere (A) per meter of conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tesla.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The physical unit defined as producing** one Newton (N) of force per meter per ampere (A)** of current flowing through it is known as** Tesla.**
 
• The derived **SI unit** of **magnetic flux density**, or the strength of a magnetic field, is the tesla (T).
 
• **One Weber per square meter** is represented by one Tesla.
 
• The **gauss** is the analogous and **obsolete cgs unit**. 
 
• There are precisely **10,000 gauss** in one Tesla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kelvin** is the unit of **temperature.**
 
• **Coulomb** is the unit of **electric charge**.
 
• **Pascal** is the unit of **pressure.**
 
• **Ampere** is the unit of **electric current.**
